No way...

BANANA CAT
Meow!

ELIAS
Wait... can everyone else see this?

RANDOM PERSON

...Nobody thinks this is weird?

VILLAIN
Citizens! Soon there will be NO BANANAS LEFT... and nothing can stop me!

Banana Cat's smile disappears.

BANANA CAT

Elias jumps on his skateboard.

Banana Cat rides on his shoulder.

Together they speed toward the giant machine as upbeat adventure music begins.

So, I am unsure if it is just me but whenever I downloaded or imported the blend files with add-on, the materials never worked like they are shown on Sketchfab. Some don't even have texture. Other file types have the same issue. Is this the problem with the site?

@TheRealDude The issue propably is that some of the models rely heavily on the HDR providing light, reflections and color. which is not included in the download, since it is not an asset the same way as the textures applied directly to models. also post processing has lot to do with how many of my uploads look.

@TheRealDude also Worth mentioning is that these highly experimental and vfx kind of models most of the time use lots of hacky ways of using the specific renderer, so they will always look somewhat or completely different when rendered with any other render engine like EEVEE or CYCLES for example. Most of the PBR textured assets usually look quite the same even when switching renderers since all the data is packed in to texture assets. But anyways. There is basically endless possibilities on why there is issues when switching tools. broken file paths in the files, broken importer, exporter, and lastly the user error.

@TheRealDude Added blender project in a zip file, you can download it as an additional file. That has similar setup as here, that the environment is reflected on this model. The HDR just is not the same as in sketchfab.

@tamminen Thanks for the quick reply. That was a massive difference between the blend file on sketchfab and the zip file. Is there any chance you can do the same for the spacedrive and space travel models? I can't find any similar model with the same quality as yours.

@TheRealDude Hi, did the same process for those models u asked. And yes, as I mentioned, the HDR is different (not colorful space), and there is no post processing used in blender (lots of saturation for example), and those factors make it look a lot different. I suggest u try to find some space HDR for your project, and then test with some post processing, and you can actually get really close as this look.

This model is over 3k tris. Significantly more than is necessary for such an asset in a PSX-style game. Preferably no more than 200 tris at the very most, and less than 120 tris at the least. Smaller details like the fixings on the payphone should be a part of the texture and not modelled. The slot at the front should also be part of the texture; even the slot itself can be a black hole. The buttons being modelled is okay, as some games in the 90s did have close-ups of smaller props at times, though the buttons being part of the texture would also suffice.

 I recommend studying the graphics of models from games like the OG Silent Hill, Syphon Filter, Resident Evil Survivor, etc, to get a feel for how props should look. Some of these models are viewable on both Sketchfab and the Models Resource for PSX/Nintendo 64 era models, and I think they'll explain better than I could lol

It's a good model, don't get me wrong, and the texture work is good too. You're a capable 3D artist, but it doesn't fit the hardware limitations of the PSX, and even calling it PS2 style is a stretch. That can break immersion. Nonetheless I appreciate you providing this asset for free!

Great model! However, the "maskmap" doesn't look right if you want to use this in unity (such as for VRChat avatars), but here's what I did to convert it into an acceptable metallic map:

Step 1: Open GIMP (prob can use photoshop too but i dont have it so idk how to do this in there)
Step 2: Load the maskmap texture
Step 2 (optional): Right click on the layer in the layers tab and hit "remove alpha channel" to better preview the image. Transparency doesn't seem to actually matter on metallic maps in unity so it shouldn't change the behavior.
Step 3: Select Colors > Saturation and drag it all the way down to desaturate the image
Step 4: Select Colors > Brightness and Contrast and set brightness to 0.035 and contrast to 0.3 (or similar, personal preference can apply)

¡Hola!

Antes de nada, quería darte la enhorabuena por este magnífico trabajo. Llevo un tiempo buscando modelos 3D de exvotos ibéricos y figuras para representar báculos y, sin duda, el tuyo es de los mejores y más fieles que he encontrado.

Formo parte de la Escuadra Íbera de la Asociación Pobladores de Elche, un grupo de recreación histórica que participa en actividades culturales y divulgativas sin ningún ánimo de lucro. Nuestro objetivo es acercar la cultura íbera al público de la forma más rigurosa posible.

Actualmente estamos preparando la recreación de un pequeño santuario íbero y nos gustaría incorporar reproducciones de exvotos para explicar cómo eran las ofrendas religiosas de la época. Tambien queremos tener varas ceremoniales coronadas por báculos. Buscamos modelos que sean lo más fieles posible a las piezas arqueológicas originales, y el tuyo encajaría perfectamente.

He visto que este modelo no tiene habilitada la descarga. Quería preguntarte si existiría la posibilidad de que nos facilitaras los archivos para poder imprimirlo en 3D. El uso sería exclusivamente cultural, educativo y sin ánimo de lucro. Por supuesto, respetaríamos la autoría del modelo y citaríamos tu trabajo siempre que fuera posible.

Si finalmente pudiéramos imprimirlo, estaríamos encantados de enviarte fotografías del resultado una vez pintado e integrado en nuestras recreaciones históricas.

Muchas gracias por tu tiempo y, de nuevo, enhorabuena por tu excelente trabajo.
